site.name: Thiruvanam Civic Authority
site.concept: Municipal civic portal for the township of Thiruvanam, custodian of heritage precincts, public works, and ward administration in the Kaveri delta.

card_pattern: Cards are framed by a thin double-line border in vermilion with a gold inner keyline, mimicking carved-pillar pairs at the left and right edges. Each card carries a small all-caps eyebrow label in peacock blue, a Yatra One title, and Lato body text. A lotus rosette acts as the bullet for list items; section corners are softened by tiny stepped notches recalling gopuram tier transitions.
design_rules: Commit hard to a tiered, dense, polychrome character drawn from Chola–Nayak temple precedent: vermilion and gold over a sacred-white ground, with peacock blue reserved for emphasis. Surfaces should feel covered, not minimal — borders, eyebrow labels, and lotus seals carry the weight. Typography is generously letter-spaced in titles to evoke stone-cut inscription, while body text remains contemporary and legible for civic use.

pages.title: Thiruvanam Civic Authority — Office of the Commissioner
pages.content_brief: Landing page introducing Thiruvanam Civic Authority, established 1947 under the Madras Municipal Act and reconstituted 1994. Hero announces the new ward roll for fiscal year 2024–25, with a stepped notice panel listing the Commissioner's address, the monthly grievance darbar (first Monday, 10:30 IST, Town Hall), and three priority programmes: Kaveri Embankment Restoration, Heritage Precinct Lighting, and the Ward 14 drainage rebuild.

pages.title: Wards & Administration — Thiruvanam Civic Authority
pages.content_brief: Lists the 27 administrative wards of Thiruvanam with elected councillor names (e.g., Tmt. R. Padmavathi, Ward 3 — Sannidhi Street; Thiru S. Arumugam, Ward 11 — Pillaiyar Koil Lane), zonal officers, and contact extensions at the Town Hall. Includes a note on the bicameral committee structure: the Standing Committee for Public Works and the Heritage & Antiquities Committee constituted under G.O. 142/2019.

pages.title: Heritage Precinct & Conservation — Thiruvanam Civic Authority
pages.content_brief: Describes the Authority's stewardship of the Old Mada Streets quadrant — granite-paved processional roads, the 1623 stone tank, and the colonnaded mandapa-market on East Veethi. Lists current conservation works: lime-mortar repointing on the southern prakara wall, polychrome restoration of the eastern arcade ceiling rosettes, and the ongoing inventory of seventeenth-century inscriptions catalogued with the Department of Archaeology, Chennai.

pages.title: Public Notices & Tenders — Thiruvanam Civic Authority
pages.content_brief: Bulletin of current public notices: tender TVN/PW/2024-31 for the rebuilding of the Kollidam culvert (closing 18 November 2024, 15:00 IST); revised property-tax assessment schedule for Zones A–C effective 1 January 2025; notification of road closure on Chitrai Veethi for the temple-car festival, 9–14 April. Each entry carries a reference number, issuing officer, and counter at which documents may be inspected.

pages.title: Services for Residents — Thiruvanam Civic Authority
pages.content_brief: Resident-facing services: birth and death registration (Counter 4, ground floor), trade licensing, water connection applications, building plan approvals under the 2016 Tamil Nadu Combined Development Rules, and the night sanitation roster. Includes the e-Sevai kiosk locations across the six revenue circles and the toll-free grievance number 1800-425-1947 staffed 06:00–22:00.

pages.title: Visit the Town Hall — Thiruvanam Civic Authority
pages.content_brief: Visitor guidance to the Town Hall, 14 Sannidhi Veethi, Thiruvanam 612 401, a 1908 granite-and-stucco building restored 2018. Public counters open Monday–Saturday 09:30–17:30, closed second Saturdays and gazetted holidays. Provides walking directions from the bus stand and the Tiruchirappalli–Thanjavur railway halt, plus accessibility notes: ramp at the western entrance, induction loop at the Commissioner's grievance hall.
